parsed.attack: The claim that the monthly bookkeeping labour is gone fails on the exception path, and that is where the graveyard's largest cluster died. Handwritten caregiver cash receipts and mileage notes are the worst input on-device OCR faces, and kill line 2 already concedes that more than 30 minutes of hand correction in half of test households kills it - this is a fiduciary accounting under a legal duty, so the first household that finds a wrong line demands verification, and the moment any person checks a statement the Zirtual wage floor is back: one reviewed household-month at a $25 loaded rate is $12.50 against a $9 subscription netting $7.65, permanently negative. On acquisition, kill line 4 accepts over 20% abandonment in sixty days, which puts cohort LTV around $60-70 against a $20-80 cost per paying user - clearing only at the very bottom of the band, and only if the sibling invite carries the second seat for free.
parsed.strongest_defence: Never employ a reviewer: flag the unclear line and let the POA sibling confirm it, which is strictly less work than the Excel rebuild they do today, so the wage floor never applies. $9/month is deliberately set below the median payer band precisely so it reads as cheaper than one hour of their own time, and a legal duty to account plus years of accumulated record makes this one of the stickier consumer subscriptions once the second year starts.
parsed.verdict_reason: The zero-labour claim survives only while the customer accepts being the corrector; the price sits below the median payer band and cohort LTV clears only the bottom of the $20-80 acquisition range.
